newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile aims to supply 20 percent of its oil needs.
newsitem.headline: Chile aims to supply 20 percent of its oil needs.

text.p: Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (Enap) expects to be able to supply 20 percent of the country's oil needs in coming years, said Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky.
A large part of Enap's production will come from its Sipetrol subsidiary which is carrying out exploration in Latin America in deals with international companies, he said.
"We think that Sipetrol which supplies today ... between three and four percent of (Enap's) oil production, could increase this to 10 percent," Teplizky told a news conference.
Enap produced 1.3 million cubic meters of crude oil in 1995, most of which came from its wells in the far southern Magellan Straits.
Sipetrol is carrying out exploration in Chile and increasing its activities in Ecuador, Colombia and Venezuela, he said.
"Sipetrol is continuing to carry out projects in Ecuador, Venezuela and Colombia, as well as the association with (Argentina's) YPF to explore in the Atlantic," said Teplizky.
"The association with state and private companies will allow Enap to develop gas and oil projects and bring (the production) to Chile with its own resources," he said.
